title: One request, two URLs: the router dispatches on the raw path while the guard reads a URL rebuilt from the unvalidated Host header
index_line: T-0065 · AUTH_DECISION · guard reads request.url.path rebuilt from Host, router uses the raw path — a path-carrying Host header separates them · python · corroborated
invariant_violated: A request has exactly one URL. The framework silently violated that: routing consumed the path as submitted, while request.url was rebuilt from an unvalidated Host header — so every guard that decided on request.url.path was guarding a different request than the one being routed.

mechanism.does: the attacker sends GET /protected with a Host value that itself carries path and query syntax the RFC forbids (Host: target.example/safe?x=)
the framework rebuilds the URL as scheme://host_header+path with no Host validation, so the reconstructed path is /safe
path-based security middleware evaluates request.url.path (/safe) and allows the request
the guard passed on one representation while the attack rides the other — nothing re-checks the raw path
the router dispatches on the raw HTTP path to the protected handler

source.http.header.value: the Host request header, accepted with path/query syntax RFC 9112 s3.2 forbids

sink.url.reconstruct.value: the scheme://host_header+path reconstruction that every request.url consumer now trusts

guard.resolve-check.value: middleware authorizing by request.url.path — defeated by feeding it the reconstructed representation

encoding.url.value: payload shape: 'example.com/safe-path?x=' prepends an attacker path inside the Host value

preconditions.expr: security middleware or endpoints decide on the reconstructed URL rather than the routed path
a path-carrying Host is accepted rather than rejected as malformed
the framework predates Host validation (starlette < 1.0.1 in the origin case; affected since 0.8.3)

check.spec: python3 -c 'import starlette, sys; print(starlette.__version__)' 2>/dev/null || pip show starlette 2>/dev/null | head -2

success: the protected route executes although the middleware's evaluated path was innocuous
status/body differ between a clean Host and a path-carrying Host on the same raw path
chained in the wild to fully unauthenticated RCE via a downstream tool's request.url-based security check
failure_like: the framework rejects a malformed Host with 400 (RFC 9112 validation present)
guards consume the same path representation the router uses
false_positive: an open redirect built from a Host-derived Location is a different record — the violated invariant here is guard-vs-router disagreement
a front-end proxy that pins Host masks the bug rather than demonstrating it

hazards: every middleware family that authorizes by URL/path: auth gates, admin-panel guards, allowlists — audit each consumer of request.url
the same reconstruction poisons redirects, reset links and server-side fetches; the sink is URL building, not any one guard
FastAPI users inherit starlette's request.url verbatim; wrappers that bolt on 'security middleware' are the prime consumers
this is T-0045's disagreement pattern moved inside a single framework — no proxy pair needed
non_transfers: frameworks that validate Host or route by the same representation they guard by
deployments behind a proxy that overwrites Host with a fixed value

evidence.target: Starlette < 1.0.1 (CVE-2026-48710 'BadHost', GHSA-86qp-5c8j-p5mr; chained in the wild with LiteLLM CVE-2026-42271 to unauthenticated RCE)

provenance.author: X41 D-Sec GmbH
provenance.corroborates: the reconstruction formula f"{scheme}://{host_header}{path}"; no RFC 9112 s3.2 validation; router depends on the raw path while request.url.path is rebuilt; PoC middleware auth bypass; affected >= 0.8.3 < 1.0.1; CWE-436; CVSS 7

provenance.author: Starlette project / pypa advisory-db (PYSEC-2026-161, GHSA-86qp-5c8j-p5mr)
provenance.corroborates: vendor confirmation: BadHost poisons request.url.path and bypasses path-based security checks; fixed in 1.0.1

provenance.author: Wiz Research
